chunk.content:
### Fixed

- `index-update` (both `--no-git` and git paths) counts a file it could not process as skipped and names it with its error, in the text output and in `--json`/`--axi` (`files_skipped`, `errors`); before, such a file vanished silently. A store that cannot return a file's hash now counts as a failed file instead of re-indexing it. (epic 20)
- `index` reports progress for an unreadable file (as skipped, with the count of files already done), and the commit-record failure message no longer begins "index updated", which a caller could read as success with a footnote. (epic 20)
- Python recursion is one rule: `self.f()` inside method `f` (and `cls.f()`) now records no self-edge, as `f()` inside `f` already did. A call to a differently named method still records its edge. An index built before this change needs `index --force`. (epic 21)
- `search` with an unquoted multi-word query no longer embeds a trailing space; the query is the arguments joined by single spaces, as `code-search`, `docs-search` and `memory-search` already did. (epic 22)
- `refs` lists every `imports` edge as unresolved. Before, an import linked to any lone chunk of the same name, so `import debounce from "lodash/debounce"` pointed at a local `function debounce` (and Go's `import "net/http"` at a lone `func http`). Re-indexing unlinks imports edges an older index had already linked. (epic 03.1)
- JavaScript and TypeScript call edges: a `this.get()` call links only to a `get` method of the caller's own class, in the same file. Before, it linked to any lone chunk named `get`, so a method was reported as a caller of a top-level function or of another class's method it can never reach. With no such method, or outside a class, the call stays unresolved in `refs` and is never shown as a caller. (epic 03.1)
- Re-indexing a file edited to remove a chunk's last call now removes that chunk's old call edges; before, an edit that left a file with no calls at all kept every edge it used to have. (epic 03)
- Opening an index written before the `file_mtime` column existed no longer fails with `no such column: file_mtime`; the migration now runs before the index that references it. (epic 11)
- Qdrant `ReadEmbeddings` reads the `Dense` vector instead of the deprecated flat `Data` field, so a server that sends only `Dense` no longer yields an empty map and forces every unchanged chunk to be re-embedded. (epic 13)
- MCP tool schemas no longer advertise `json` and `min` properties. The server always runs the CLI with `--axi`, so setting either was silently ignored. (epic 08)

- With `--axi`, a failed command now prints its error as TOON (`error: true`, `message: ...`) on stdout and still exits non-zero. Before this it printed a plain `Error: ...` on stderr and left stdout empty, because nothing passed `--axi` to the error formatter. This covers errors from the root command's config checks as well as from the subcommand. (epic 05.1)
- Plain `multisearch` with `--output by_query` or `by_collection` no longer prints `No results found.` under a header that counts results. The empty check read the blended list, which a grouped format leaves empty; it now reads the total. (epic 05.1)
- `search`, the profile search aliases and `multisearch` over an index that exists but holds no chunks no longer print `No results found for "..."`, the same words as a search that matched nothing. They say the index is empty and name `llm-semantic index <path>`; in `--axi` the answer carries `status: index_empty` and a `help` list pointing at `index`. An empty answer over a populated index carries `status: no_match`. `--json` is unchanged. (epic 05.1)
